rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word al-ḥaqq is accusative because an governing verb is suppressed.
rows.anchor: The word َّقَحْال is in the accusative because of a suppressed verb.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible speaker of the reply is those whose fate is being decided; truth will be so evident that no one can claim injustice.
rows.anchor: The reply can possibly be from two people. It can be from those whose final fate will be settled on that day

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the reply may come from those spared that day's terror; if so, most people will be absorbed in themselves while the protected affirm God's verdict and expose the futility of hoped-for intercession.
rows.anchor: The reply can also be from people who were held secure from the horror of that day

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted and powerful; no one may speak before Him without permission or has the capacity to reach Him.
rows.anchor: No one can dare open his tongue before Him without His permission nor does anyone have the caliber to access Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even Gabriel, the highest-ranking angel, cannot approach God; a cited couplet says his wings would burn if he advanced even a hair's breadth amid divine disclosures.
rows.anchor: Among angels, Gabriel occupies the highest status before God; yet he too is helpless in accessing God’s presence:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questions ask who provides livelihood, rain, seasons, and growing crops; the answer is God, whose control of heaven and earth shows one powerful ruler.
rows.anchor: Who in the heavens and the earth gives livelihood to them? Who sends down rain from the sky and causes various seasons?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God supplies the answer because the addressees cannot deny it: Makkan idolaters treated their deities as intercessors, not creators or providers, and acknowledged God as provider.
rows.anchor: the Idolaters of Makkah never regarded any of their deities to be the creator or provider; they only regarded them as intercessors

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternatives of guidance or manifest error declare that if the audience disputes this acknowledged truth, debate is futile and God will decide who is guided; Islahi reads this as prophetic disavowal, not tolerance.
rows.anchor: In my opinion, this is a statement of acquittal from the Prophet (sws) and not an expression of tolerance, as is generally understood.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When addressees stubbornly deny obvious facts, the Prophet is told further discussion has no purpose and each side should persist in its own way.
rows.anchor: The background is that when the addressees try to deny obvious facts because of stubbornness and arrogance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same disavowal appears in 42:15, where each party keeps its deeds, and in 109:6, where each keeps its religion.
rows.anchor: Our deeds will be with us and your deeds will be with you; no discussion is now needed among us.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic declarations of separation address stubborn rejection of obvious facts; contextualizing them shows acquittal and aversion, not tolerance or accommodation.
rows.anchor: they do not express tolerance; they portray acquittal and aversion.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the audience rejects the message, God will gather both sides and judge justly; His knowledge is complete and none can dispute His verdict.
rows.anchor: God will gather both factions and then pass His Judgement with justice. He is the greatest judge; no one has the power to dispute His verdicts

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge to show God's alleged partners repeats the earlier argument with sarcasm, rebuke, and warning.
rows.anchor: Exuding from this style is sarcasm, rebuke and warning. They are dared to show what they worship besides God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge is answered by denying any partner of God's status; His might and wisdom confirm that no such partner exists.
rows.anchor: there is no one of this status that he becomes God’s partner. God’s acknowledged attributes are then cited to bolster this refutation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the passage's background, the righteous realize and refine their capacities while the truth is conclusively delivered to wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: potentials of the righteous materialize and are polished and the truth is conclusively delivered to the wrong-doers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spiritually lifeless are blind to the call and will not accept it however much the Prophet tries.
rows.anchor: become lifeless will not accept his call however much an effort he makes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This contrast reassures the Prophet that responses will differ: only people with insight benefit from his light, while spiritually lifeless people will not accept his call despite his effort.
rows.anchor: Only those people will benefit from the radiance of the light he has who have insight in them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's law enhances the insight and guidance of people who value their innate abilities, while those who neglect them are deprived even of those abilities.
rows.anchor: It is the law of the Almighty that those who keep alive and duly value their innate abilities find that their insight and guidance has been enhanced

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Darkness/light and heat/shade parallel the unequal human types just mentioned, and the counterparts together serve the world's collective benefit.
rows.anchor: The verses state that just as there is darkness and light in this world and heat and shade as well

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world's collective benefit requires free will; therefore those who neglect God's capacities and follow falsehood are given respite for a period.
rows.anchor: this world has been created by God to test the free-will of man hence wisdom entails that those people also be given respite till a certain period of time

rows.speaker: Some scholars
rows.claim: Some scholars consider the repeated lā superfluous; Islahi rejects that view and says its recurrence emphasizes the contrast.
rows.anchor: Some scholars regard the recurrence of َلَا as superfluous. In my opinion, this is not so. Its recurrence is meant for emphasis.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet worried that his people's indifference reflected a shortcoming in him; God reassures him that he must address the living, while the spiritually and intellectually dead will not respond however much he wishes.
rows.anchor: To dispel this worry, the Almighty has assured him through various styles in this verse. He is told that his duty is to make the living listen to his message and not the dead.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here 'making hear' means urging and propelling someone to hear and accept.
rows.anchor: the word سماعإِ means to urge and propel someone to hear and accept something.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants the urge to listen and understand according to His wisdom: people who preserve their natural abilities receive it, while those who neglect them become morally and spiritually dead and can be revived only by God.
rows.anchor: those who keep alive the natural abilities bestowed to them by Him find in themselves the divinely given urge to listen and understand further.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's responsibility is only to warn of danger and convey truth, glad tidings, and warnings; he is not responsible for making everyone accept the message.
rows.anchor: he is only liable to inform them of the looming danger; he is not liable to make everyone accept his message.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every earlier community also received a warner, whose story guides the Prophet and his people: God will deal with him and his nation as He dealt with prior messengers and nations.
rows.anchor: God Has sent warners among previous nations as well and there is guidance for him and his people in the account of these warners.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier nations also rejected their messengers, so the Prophet should see rejection as a recurring pattern rather than evidence that he made a mistake.
rows.anchor: Earlier nations too rejected their respective messengers. This is an age old tradition.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier messengers brought clear proofs, miracles, scriptures, and God's clear Book, yet these signs could not convince their audiences; requested signs likewise will not make stubborn hearers believe.
rows.anchor: they came with very lucid proofs, miracles, scriptures and with the clear Book of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-bayyināt and al-zubur have general meanings and describe what all God's messengers were sent with.
rows.anchor: The words ِاتَنِّیَبْال andِرُبُّالز have a general connotation. All messengers of God were sent with them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The 'luminous Book' refers to the Torah, which held the status of the clear Book before the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: however refers to the Torah, as before the Qur’ān, it was the Torah that occupied the status of the lucid Book.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God seized rejecting nations with exemplary punishment; the same law will apply to Muhammad's people if they persist obstinately.
rows.anchor: when they reject their respective messenger, the Almighty seized them and what an exemplary punishment He meted out to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 27 explains through further examples in the universe the reality already communicated in verses 20–22.
rows.anchor: The reality that is communicated earlier in verses 20-22 is once again explained here in the light of some other examples found in this universe.
